The ASV spends a single English word on the preposition and the negative substantive together: from carries both the privative relation of the lamed and the negation of biltiy, which is why the clause reads stay from having rather than stay to have. Rule 30's one-rendering condition is therefore met and the two morphemes share one unit, headed on the negation, exactly as rule 48's closing sentence directs for a min-beli the ASV renders by one word. The previous reading marked biltiy unrepresented while its own note conceded that the negation is absorbed in from, which is what rules 22 and 30 forbid for a morpheme whose sense the ASV has written inside a fused word.
